title: llm usage_rules is labelled v2 parity and answers about a different file than v2
body:
CLASS: a behaviour change shipped under a PARITY label, invisible in the one checkout everybody drives.

`render.rs:6780` opens `intent llm usage_rules -- v2 parity: the project's root usage-rules.md, verbatim, on stdout (AC-00.3)`. v2 does not read the project's root file. `bin/intent_llm` reads `$INTENT_HOME/usage-rules.md` -- the INSTALL's copy -- and `$INTENT_HOME` is set at `bin/intent:31` to the directory above `bin/`, never to `PROJECT_ROOT`.

DRIVEN 2026-09-02 18:09Z (dc), two scratch projects, both binaries, no pipes in the rc reads:

- Project WITH its own 78-byte root `usage-rules.md`: v2 rc=0 printing the INSTALL's 20,220 bytes (`# Intent Usage Rules`); v3 rc=0 printing the PROJECT's 78 bytes. Same command, same directory, different file.
- Project WITHOUT a root `usage-rules.md`: **v2 rc=0 with 20,220 bytes; v3 rc=1 with nothing** (`error: this project has no usage-rules.md at its root`). An exit-code flip on a shipped verb.

**THE v3 BEHAVIOUR IS THE RIGHT ONE AND ITS REASONING IS SOUND** -- the file is user-owned, `canon::seed` writes it only when absent, and rendering the template would silently print rules a project has edited away from. The doc comment argues all of that correctly. What is wrong is the word `parity`, and what is missing is anyone having compared the two.

**WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: IN A SELF-HOSTED CHECKOUT THE INSTALL ROOT AND THE PROJECT ROOT ARE THE SAME DIRECTORY**, so `$INTENT_HOME/usage-rules.md` and `<project>/usage-rules.md` are one file and every drive taken here agrees. The divergence exists only in a project that is not Intent, which is every consumer.

**AND THE ROSTER ROW COULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT EITHER**: the entry's `evidence_class` is `read` -- *taken from the v2 source at the stamped revision without executing that specific arm*.

SEVERITY: filed medium, and the case for high is the rc flip rather than the content difference -- a consumer scripting `intent llm usage_rules` gets a non-zero exit where v2 gave zero. vc to rule.

REMEDY IS A LABEL AND A NOTE, NOT A CODE CHANGE (recommended): keep the behaviour, strike `v2 parity` from `render.rs:6780`, say plainly that v3 deliberately answers about the PROJECT where v2 answered about the INSTALL, and give the migration its line -- a project with no root `usage-rules.md` now gets rc=1 with a remedy instead of the tool's own rules. If the divergence is instead to be closed toward v2, that is a product call and hv's.

OWNER: ic (WP-09, the `llm` family). FOUND while reading 0181 to dispose of `llm usage_rules --symlink`; recorded separately rather than folded into it, because the flag is a scope decision and this is a shipped-artefact claim.

**REMEDY APPLIED 2026-09-02 (ic, WP-09's owner).** The `v2 parity` label is struck from `render.rs`; the doc comment now says plainly that v3 answers about the PROJECT where v2 answered about the INSTALL, carries dc's two-project measurement, and states the self-hosting collision as the reason it survived. The migration note is at `docs/migrating-from-v2.md`, with the rc flip in a table a consumer can script against and a pointer to `intent claude upgrade --apply` for the second row.

**dc's v2 source claim was verified independently before the label was changed**, rather than taken on the strength of the report: `bin/intent_llm:55` sets `USAGE_RULES_FILE="$INTENT_HOME/usage-rules.md"` and `bin/intent:31` resolves `INTENT_HOME` to the directory above `bin/`. The behaviour is what dc measured.

**LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY, WITH TWO THINGS OUTSTANDING AND NEITHER OF THEM MINE.** vc has the severity call -- the case for high is the rc flip rather than the content difference. And dc named an alternative to the remedy: *if the divergence is instead to be closed toward v2, that is a product call and hv's.* **Closing this row on the strength of the label being fixed would bury that question**, which is the one an operator scripting the verb actually cares about.
=== RULED HIGH 2026-09-02 19:50Z (vc, under hv's pen). READ THE REST OF THIS BEFORE ACTING ON THE SEVERITY ===

**HIGH DOES NOT MEAN REVERT v3, AND THIS PARAGRAPH EXISTS BECAUSE IT WOULD OTHERWISE BE READ THAT WAY.** The v3 behaviour STAYS EXACTLY AS IT IS. It is the correct answer and its doc comment argues it correctly: the file is user-owned, `canon::seed` writes it only when absent, and rendering the template instead would silently print rules a project has deliberately edited away from. **Nothing here asks for a line of behaviour to change.**

**WHAT IS HIGH IS THE WORD `parity` AND THE FACT THAT NOBODY HAD COMPARED THE TWO.** The remedy is a label, a comparison, and a migration note. If a later reader takes this row as licence to point v3 back at `$INTENT_HOME/usage-rules.md`, they have inverted it.

**GROUND ONE, WHICH SETS THE FLOOR: AN EXIT-CODE FLIP ON A SHIPPED VERB.** Same project, no root `usage-rules.md`: v2 rc=0 with 20,220 bytes, v3 rc=1 with nothing. Anything scripting this verb breaks on upgrade, and the rc is the sharper fact than the content difference.

**GROUND TWO, WHICH IS WHAT MOVES IT OFF MEDIUM: THE ESTATE STRUCTURALLY CANNOT REPRODUCE IT.** Driven here -- `~/.intent/usage-rules.md` does not exist, `./usage-rules.md` does at 20,220 bytes, exactly the figure v2 emitted -- so in this self-hosted checkout `$INTENT_HOME/usage-rules.md` and the project's root file are ONE FILE UNDER TWO NAMES, and **every drive taken in this tree agrees by construction.**

**A DEFECT THE ESTATE CANNOT REPRODUCE IS ONE A USER FINDS, NOT ONE WE FIND.** That is a severity argument rather than an elegant observation: **our detection probability here is zero and stays zero however carefully anyone works.** Same family as `--workspace` against `--all-targets` -- an instrument whose population cannot contain the class -- except that this one is a property of the whole checkout rather than of one command, so it applies to every `v2:`-labelled row whose evidence was taken by driving both binaries here.

=== THE `v2:` CENSUS, RUN 2026-09-02 21:13Z (dc). THE CLASS HAS EXACTLY ONE MEMBER AND IT IS THIS ROW ===

**A NEGATIVE RESULT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF RUNNING IT.** The question was: which parity rows' evidence could be wrong because a drive taken in this checkout cannot tell the install root from the project root? **Answer: one, and it is already filed.**

**THE POPULATION.** 138 dispatch-table entries carry a `v2:` field -- 44 `measured`, 37 `read`, 57 declaring no `evidence_class`. Counted structurally, walking the objects.

**THE v2 SIDE.** 161 lines in the v2 trunk mention `INTENT_HOME`; **91 are a resolution of the form `$INTENT_HOME/<path>`.** Of those:

- **65 locate the tool's own code** -- `bin/...` (61) and `lib/...` (4). **A project has neither shape, so they cannot collide at all**: the install is the install in a self-hosted checkout and in any other, and both resolve identically.
- **26 are project-shaped by prefix**, across 20 distinct paths -- mostly `intent/plugins/...`, plus `agents/.manifest/...`, `README.md` and `usage-rules.md`.

**THE INSTRUMENT: DOES A REAL PROJECT ACTUALLY CARRY THE PATH?** Driven against a fresh tree built with `intent init` + `intent claude upgrade --apply`, rather than reasoned from the shape. **Exactly ONE of the 20 is present: `usage-rules.md`** (`bin/intent_llm:55`). Every `intent/plugins/...` path is absent -- a project's `intent/` holds `llm/` and `wip.md`, never `plugins/`.

**TWO CONTROLS, BOTH PASSING.** Negative: `bin/intent_helpers` is absent from a project, as the install-only classification requires. Positive: `usage-rules.md` is present -- **this row's own confirmed instance, which the instrument had to find or be discarded.**

**AND TWO OF THE 20 ARE NOT READS AT ALL.** `intent_help:142-143` expands `$INTENT_HOME/README.md` and `$INTENT_HOME/intent/docs/` **inside a heredoc, as text printed to the user.** A printed path cannot pick the wrong file; the string is correct in a self-hosted checkout and in any other. They are candidates by shape and not by mechanism.

**THE v3 SIDE, WHICH IS WHY THE CLASS CANNOT GROW.** v3 reads **no** `INTENT_HOME` at all, and that is guarded rather than merely true: `no_intent_home.rs` (AT-11.3 / AC-11.3) is an ALLOWLIST control over the environment the shipped surface may read. **So there is no v3 install-root resolution for any content**, and the divergence can only arise where v2 reads the install for something v3 reads from the project. Across all of v3's source, the project root is joined to exactly six names: `usage-rules.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.intent_critic.yml`, `.prettierignore`, `.gitignore`, `intent/st/ST0056/tui-design.md`. **Intersected with the v2 `$INTENT_HOME` reads, the answer is `usage-rules.md` and nothing else.**

**AND THE GUARD'S OWN HEADER STATES THIS EXACT CLASS, ELEVEN DAYS BEFORE THE CENSUS RAN:** *If v3 had inherited that dependency, every developer machine here would still be green, because every developer machine here has it set.* **The estate had already named the shape -- an environment property that makes a defect unobservable locally -- and built a control for that instance of it.** This census is the same question asked of the parity register rather than of the environment.

**WHAT THE CENSUS DOES NOT CLAIM.** It covers the install-versus-project collision only. A `v2:` row can still be wrong for any of the ordinary reasons -- and 57 of the 138 declare no `evidence_class` at all, which is a different gap and a larger one.
